rulings.Case Title: RANDALL GARY HUCK VS. KAISER FOUNDATION HEALTH PLAN INC. ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Hearing On Petition To Vacate Contractual Arbitration Award
rulings.Rulings: Matter on the Law & Motion and Discovery Calendar for Friday, July 31, 2026, Line 1, PETITIONER RANDALL HUCK's Petition To Vacate Contractual Arbitration Award. Petitioner Randall Huck's petition to vacate arbitration award is denied. Huck fails to show any of the limited grounds available to vacate an arbitration award. CCP 1286.2(a)(5), the sole basis asserted by Huck to vacate the award, is inapplicable because Huck has not shown that the Arbitrator refused to postpone the arbitration hearing, refused to hear material evidence, or committed any conduct violative of the California Arbitration Act nor has Huck shown that he was substantially prejudiced by any conduct of the Arbitrator. The decision of whether and when to hold a hearing on Huck's post-award reconsideration motion was within the Arbitrator's discretion and is not a basis to vacate an award. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 301 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 301 Zoom ID 161 502 4290; Passcode 700956.) To appear remotely at the hearing, go to the court's website at sfsuperiorcourt.org under "Online Services," navigate to "Tentative Rulings," and click on the appropriate link, or dial the corresponding phone number. Any party who contests a tentative ruling must send an email to contestdept301tr@sftc.org with a copy to all other parties by 4pm stating, without argument, the portion(s) of the tentative ruling that the party contests. The subject line of the email shall include the line number, case name and case number. The text of the email shall include the name and contact information, including email address, of the attorney or party who will appear at the hearing. Counsel for the prevailing party is required to prepare a proposed order which repeats verbatim the substantive portion of the tentative ruling and must email it to contestdept301tr@sftc.org prior to the hearing even if the tentative ruling is not contested. rulings.Case Title: BRYANT FU VS. SHUZHEN TU ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion For Terminating Sanctions Against Defendant Legal Recover Llc
rulings.Rulings: Matter on the Law & Motion and Discovery Calendar for Friday, July 31, 2026, Line 2, PLAINTIFF BRYANT FU's Motion For Terminating Sanctions Against Defendant Legal Recover LLC. Plaintiff Bryant Fu's motion for terminating sanctions against defendant Legal Recover LLC is denied. While Fu has shown that Legal Recover and its affiliates have engaged in discovery abuse in the past, Legal Recover's responses to his requests for production of documents are not code-compliant and its failure to produce Ms. Yan for deposition is arguably another discovery violation, Fu has not shown that there are no lesser alternatives to terminating sanctions to remediate any prejudice the claims to have suffered. Moreover, Fu's principal argument appears to be that he believes Legal Recover discovery responses are false and made in bad faith. That argument is best addressed by the trial judge by a motion in limine or otherwise. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 301 remotely or in person. rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion To Compel Defendant Andrea Flora Augustin To Provide Further Responses To Special Interrogatories, Form Interrogatories, Requests For Admission, And Requests For Production Of Documents, Set One; And For Monetary Sanctions; Memorandum Of Points And Authorities In Support Thereof
rulings.Rulings: Matter on the Law & Motion and Discovery Calendar for Friday, July 31, 2026, Line 5, PLAINTIFF LIUDMILA NAUMIK's Motion To Compel Defendant Andrea Flora Augustin To Provide Further Responses To Special Interrogatories, Form Interrogatories, Requests For Admission, And Requests For Production Of Documents, Set One; And For Monetary Sanctions. Plaintiff Liudmila Naumik's motion to compel defendant Andrea Augustin to provide further responses to special interrogatories, form interrogatories, requests for admission and requests for production of documents is denied as moot and her request for monetary sanctions is granted in small part. No later than August 14, 2026 Augustin must pay $1,060 in monetary sanctions to Naumik. Augustin's service of supplemental responses to the great majority of discovery requests that Naumik sought supplemental responses moots this motion. If Naumik believes that the supplemental responses are deficient, she must engage in a code-compliant meet and confer with Augustin's counsel and, if any issues remain unresolved after the meet and confer, she may file another motion to compel. Augustin's service of supplemental responses on the same day as her opposition papers is a tacit admission that her prior responses were not made in good faith and lacked substantial justification. As a self-represented litigant, sanctions awarded to Naumik are limited to $1,000 per CCP 2030.50 and her out of pocket costs. (Damak v. Superior Court (July 8, 2026 Fourth District Court of Appeal) 2026 WL 1971200). For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 301 remotely or in person. rulings.Rulings: Matter on the Law & Motion and Discovery Calendar for Friday, July 31, 2026, Line 7, PLAINTIFF ATHECIA SANCHEZ'S MOTION TO QUASH SUBPOENAS. Plaintiff Athecia Sanchez' motion to quash subpoenas is granted in part. The subpoenas seeking billing records are quashed. The subpoenas seeking medical records are limited to the following medical records: a) all medical records relating to the accident on December 14, 2024 and b) all medical records relating to the Walter Castillo being under the influence of alcohol or any illegal substances from January 18, 2014 through December 1r, 2024. The City has not shown that any of the billing records are directly relevant to the issues in this case. The only medical records that the City has shown that are directly relevant to the issues in this case are those relating to the December 14, 2024 accident and alcohol and other substance abuse from January 18, 2014, the date of the police report attached as K to the Wald declaration, to Castillo's date of death. The City may seek billing records and additional medical records by subpoena later in the case if and when they are able to show those records are directly relevant to the issues in this case. rulings.Case Title: JACKIE FORGE VS. DON JOSE BARRELIER ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Motion For Order Compelling Further Responses To Request For Admissionss, Set One; Memorandum Of Points And Authorities In Support
rulings.Rulings: Matter on the Law & Motion and Discovery Calendar for Friday, July 31, 2026, Line 10, 2- PLAINTIFF JACKIE FORGE's Motion For Order Compelling Further Responses To Request For Admissionss, Set One. Plaintiff Jackie Forge's motion to compel further responses to her set one requests for admissions and for monetary sanctions is granted in large part. No later than August 20, 2026 defendant Don Jose Barrelier must serve verified further code-compliant responses to requests 4-17 and 27-28 without objections and pay reasonable monetary sanctions of $1,560 to Forge. Barrelier's response to requests 4-17 and 27-28 are insufficient, not code-compliant, and evasive. All of the objections to these requests lack merit. Poorly drafted requests must be properly responded to where, as here, it is reasonably clear what the request is asking. Responding with the word "appears" is not code-compliant. Responding subject to objections is not code-compliant. The requests seek discovery relevant information and should have been responded with admit, deny, or unable to admit or deny. Barrelier's responses to requests 4-17 and 28-28 lack substantial justification. Reasonable monetary sanctions are calculated at three hours at $500 per hour plus the filing fee for this motion.
